messages:
Maria: hey team — posting the latest mock for the \"Chronicle\" compact version history panel. want quick eyes on the copy + rollback affordance before i hand to devs :eyes: Maria: link to figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/chronicle-compact — page: compact-versions-v3 Kevin: saw it, looks sleek. main ask: we need clear canary indicators (traffic %) and an obvious fallback flow for failed rollouts. Joel: fyi rendering hundreds of versions might kill initial paint on older machines. we should virtualize the list or collapse older entries into a \"past\" group. Maria: agreed re collapse. thinking: show latest 10 + a \"Load more (archived)\" row. that keeps timeline compact. Lina: microinteraction thought: on keyboard focus, show a tippy preview with commit message & diffs summary. must be reachable with tab only. Tal: copy nits: the rollback button currently reads \"Rollback to this\" — sounds aggressive. suggest alternatives: `Revert to vX`, `Restore vX`, `Switch to vX`. shorter is better for small buttons. Kevin: +1 to \"Restore vX\" — less scary for non-technical PMs/customers. Joel: implementation note: rollback is multi-step server side. frontend should grey out the button after click and surface progress + cancel. also keyboard confirmation required for a11y. Maria: ok so candidate copy: `Restore to v1.4.2` for primary action, confirmation modal header: `Restore version v1.4.2?` body: `This will route new traffic to v1.4.2. Ongoing requests will finish on the current version.` Tal: prefer modal copy to explicitly mention canary traffic behavior when applicable. e.g., `This will route X% of traffic back to v1.4.2.` Lina: accessibility nit: modal must trap focus, announce via aria-live region, and the primary action button should be first in the tab order so keyboard users can commit without reaching the secondary by accident. Also need visible focus ring on the miniature timeline items. Maria: good call. Lina, can you paste an example aria snippet? Lina: sure — quick example: ```
\n

Restore version v1.4.2?

\n
Routing: 100% to v1.4.2
\n \n \n
``` Maria: perfect. also thinking about the version badges — small colored pill showing canary/active/archived. color contrast needs to meet AA. Tal, can you run contrast checks? Tal: will do. if we use current teal for active it fails with white text at small sizes. propose darker teal or bold text with outline. Joel: backlog item: when canary is <5% traffic, we shouldn't show big progress bars — just a micro sparkline + percentage. heavy visuals = noise. Kevin: agree, keep the visual weight proportional to impact. also for A/B experiments we need to show variant labels and confidence metric (e.g., CTR delta). where does that live? inside expanded details? Maria: plan: compact row shows version id, timestamp, small badge, traffic % (if >0), and a chevron to expand details (diff, metrics, rollout controls). Lina: keyboard users need a 2-step expand: Enter to open, Esc to close, arrow keys to navigate adjacent rows. please document these keybindings in docs. Joel: + note: virtualization + expansion panels is tricky (need to keep focused element mounted). we'll schedule a spike. DeployBot: ticket created — RED-3245: \"Compact Chronicle: virtualization + a11y + rollback modal\" — https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RED-3245 :white_check_mark: Maria: thanks @DeployBot — action items for me: update figma with \"Restore\" copy and keyboard flows. Lina: implement aria example + focus rules. Joel: spike virtualization and share perf numbers. Tal: contrast + canary visual specs. Kevin: confirm metrics to show in expanded details (confidence, traffic, error rate). Kevin: i'll send the metrics list by EOD. Maria: cool. tiny remaining copy decision — confirmation CTA label: \"Restore\" vs \"Confirm restore\"? shorter wins in tight modal. leaning \"Restore\". Tal: \"Restore\" is fine, but ensure screen reader context: add `aria-label=\"Restore version v1.4.2\"` to button. Lina: will add that and document in the PR checklist. Maria: thanks all — i'll ping again after i update the mock. :sparkles:
